title: Sequential finite-free presentation of a countably generated flat Mittag-Leffler module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ an $R$-module that is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], Mittag-Leffler [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], and generated by an at most countable subset under finite $R$-linear combinations. There exist $R$-modules $G_n$, maps $u_n:G_n\to G_{n+1}$ and $\iota_n:G_n\to P$ for integers $n\ge1$, and integers $r_n\ge0$, such that $G_n\cong R^{r_n}$, $\iota_{n+1}u_n=\iota_n$, and $(P,(\iota_n))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in $R$-modules of $G_1\xrightarrow{u_1}G_2\xrightarrow{u_2}\cdots$. Here $R^{r_n}$ is the module of $r_n$-tuples with componentwise operations; the transition maps need not be injective.

source.place: Tag 059X (lemma-countgen-projective), opening paragraph, together with Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit) and the paragraph immediately following it.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring with $P$ preserves exactness and initial injectivity; [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] supplies terminal surjectivity. Thus $-\otimes_RP$ preserves short exact sequences, exactly the hypothesis of [lem-kun-lazard-flat-module]. Apply it to obtain a small nonempty directed poset $I$, finite-free modules $F_i\cong R^{r_i}$, transition maps $f_{ij}$, and compatible maps $a_i:F_i\to P$ making $P$ their colimit.

Each $F_i\cong R^{r_i}$ is finitely presented: it is the cokernel of the zero map $R^0\to R^{r_i}$, transported across the given isomorphism. All hypotheses of [lem-trf-ml-countable-colimit] now hold: $I$ is small, nonempty and directed, the cocone has vertex $P$, and $P$ is Mittag-Leffler and at most countably generated by assumption. Obtain a nonempty at most countable directed subset $J\subseteq I$ such that the restricted cocone still has colimit $P$. Indeed the canonical map from its colimit to $P$ is an isomorphism, so composition with this isomorphism gives the same universal property.

Enumerate $J$ by a sequence $b_1,b_2,\ldots$ containing every element, repeating elements if $J$ is finite; nonemptiness permits padding. Define $j_1=b_1$ and choose $j_{n+1}\in J$ above both $j_n$ and $b_{n+1}$ using directedness. Induction gives $j_n\le j_{n+1}$ and $b_n\le j_n$. Hence for every $i\in J$ some $n$ satisfies $i\le j_n$. Put $G_n=F_{j_n}$, $u_n=f_{j_n,j_{n+1}}$, $\iota_n=a_{j_n}$ and $r_n=r_{j_n}$. Then $G_n\cong R^{r_n}$ and $\iota_{n+1}u_n=\iota_n$ by cocone compatibility. No strict increase or injectivity of $u_n$ is required.

source.place: Paragraph immediately after Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit); the recursive upper-bound construction in Tag 0597 (lemma-ML-limit-nonempty).

proof.text: Verify the sequential colimit using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given a compatible cocone $h_n:G_n\to N$, for each $i\in J$ choose $n$ with $i\le j_n$ and set $h_i=h_n f_{i,j_n}$. This is independent of $n$: for two choices $n,m$, take $l\ge n,m$; compatibility along the finite composites of the $u_k$ identifies both expressions with $h_l f_{i,j_l}$. For $i\le k$ in $J$, choose $n$ with $k\le j_n$; then $h_k f_{ik}=h_n f_{k,j_n}f_{ik}=h_n f_{i,j_n}=h_i$. Thus these maps form a cocone over $J$. Its restriction at $j_n$ is the original $h_n$, by taking $n$ itself in the defining formula. Step 2 gives a unique $h:P\to N$ with $h a_i=h_i$ for every $i\in J$, hence $h\iota_n=h_n$. Conversely any map satisfying these sequential equations satisfies $h a_i=h\iota_n f_{i,j_n}=h_n f_{i,j_n}=h_i$ whenever $i\le j_n$, so uniqueness over $J$ proves sequential uniqueness. Therefore $(P,(\iota_n))$ is the required colimit.

lean.statement: theorem exists_sequential_finite_free_presentation_of_flat_isMittagLeffler (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (P : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Flat R P] (hML : Module.IsMittagLeffler.{u, max u v, max u v, 0} R P) (hcountable : ∃ E : Set P, E.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R E = ⊤) : ∃ (G : ℕ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (ι : G ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj (ModuleCat.of R P)) (r : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((G.obj n) ≃ₗ[R] (Fin (r n) → R))) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk (ModuleCat.of R P) ι))
